case_title: Major Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (nephew of the deceased); prior quarrel the previous day in which the victim reprimanded the accused
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (charged; High Court conviction, set aside); IPC s.304 Part II (conviction in Supreme Court)
weapon: Wooden 'Bahi' (wooden side of a cot frame)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (two sons of the victim); medical (post-mortem); recovery of the weapon following the accused's disclosure
confession: Police-recorded disclosure of where the weapon was hidden, leading to its recovery; the Supreme Court noted the recovery followed the confession (para 12) as part of the evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Blow with great force to the head of an elderly man, causing skull fracture (High Court's view); grudge from the previous day's quarrel
mitigating_circumstances: Provocation from the victim's yelling the previous day; weapon not dangerous; single blow; no intention or knowledge that death would result
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of s.302 IPC on 13.07.2001 (delay in FIR, weak motive, unreliable eyewitnesses, medical contradictions, site plan discrepancies)
high_court_outcome: Acquittal set aside; convicted under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 (03.04.2014)
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s.304 Part II
neutral_facts: On the day before the incident, the accused quarrelled with the victim, who was the accused's uncle, and abused him; the victim sharply reprimanded the accused. The next morning, at about 10:30 to 11:00 a.m., the victim was walking towards the village bus stand when the accused approached from the opposite direction carrying a wooden side of a cot frame. The accused abused the victim for shouting at and insulting him the previous day, said he would teach him a lesson, and struck the victim once on the head. The victim fell down, and the accused ran away with the wooden piece. Two of the victim's sons, who were standing outside a nearby shop, took their bleeding father to Civil Hospital, Giddarbaha, from where he was referred to Dayanand Medical College, Ludhiana. The victim died the following day. The complainant son gave a written statement to a police officer, which was endorsed and sent for registration of an FIR. Police visited the spot, prepared a rough site plan and lifted blood-stained earth. At the hospital, an inquest was prepared, and a post-mortem found eight injuries, the main one on the head; the doctor opined the cause of death was shock and haemorrhage from the head injury. The accused was arrested some weeks later and, in police presence, indicated where the blood-stained wooden piece was concealed in a wheat chaff room at the accused's residence; it was recovered. Chemical examination found the blood on the piece and on the spot earth matched the victim. Two eyewitnesses, the victim's sons, testified that the accused struck the victim's head with the wooden piece.
physical_harm: Single blow to the victim's head causing skull fracture (as found by High Court); eight injuries in total on post-mortem; death the next day from shock and haemorrhage due to head injury
number_of_offences: 1 charged; 1 conviction stands (s.304 Part II, altered from s.302)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Supreme Court. The High Court had reasoned the occurrence was not sudden and had a grudge behind it, but the Supreme Court found no intention to kill and did not find premeditation.
motive: Anger and provocation from the victim's reprimand and yelling the previous day (accepted by the Supreme Court)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness accounts of the two sons; post-mortem evidence of head injury as cause of death; recovery of the blood-stained 'Bahi' with chemical match to the victim's blood
witness_credibility: High Court found the eyewitness version truthful and trustworthy; the Supreme Court accepted the occurrence as proved beyond reasonable doubt and did not disturb this
post_offence_conduct: Fled the spot with the weapon; concealed the 'Bahi' at his residence; arrested on 09.08.1998; the disclosure led to recovery of the weapon
custody_duration: Arrested 09.08.1998; released 13.07.2001 after trial court acquittal; surrendered 04.10.2014; more than eight years' incarceration per the Court
trial_duration: offence: 21.07.1998 (incident; quarrel the previous day, 20.07.1998); trial judgment: 13.07.2001; High Court: 03.04.2014; Supreme Court: 16.06.2022
legal_representation: Accused-appellant: Gagan Gupta. Respondents (State of Punjab & Anr.): R. K. Rathore and Ms. Jaspreet Gogia
investigation_status: FIR registered; site visit, rough site plan, blood-stained earth lifted; inquest and post-mortem done; arrest and recovery made; case committed to Sessions; charge framed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Trial court flagged a 4½-hour FIR delay and late arrest; the High Court found no reason to disbelieve the prosecution on these grounds; the Supreme Court raised no separate irregularity
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted of s.302 (13.07.2001). High Court: acquittal set aside, convicted under s.302, life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine (03.04.2014). Supreme Court: partly allowed; s.302 conviction set aside; convicted under s.304 Part II; sentence reduced to period already undergone; fine retained
defence_argument: Alternatively, the offence was culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 IPC rather than murder under s.302
legal_principle_applied: Distinction between culpable homicide amounting to murder (s.302) and culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304); intention is pivotal, with knowledge and the degree of the act also relevant; factors from Pulicherla Nagaraju applied
precedent_relied_upon: Mohd. Rafiq v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2021) 10 SCC 706 (relying on State of Andhra Pradesh v. Rayavarapu Punnayya and Pulicherla Nagaraju @ Nagaraja Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh)
sentencing_rationale: Conviction altered to s.304 Part II because the accused lacked intention to kill and knowledge of likely death; sentence reduced in view of more than eight years already served
judicial_mitigating_factors: No intention to kill; provocation by the uncle's reprimand the previous day; non-dangerous weapon; single blow; no knowledge that a single blow would cause death; period already undergone
other_sentence_order: Release forthwith if not wanted in any other criminal case; fine of Rs.5,000 remains as imposed by the High Court
